paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: La clase va a empezar dentro de poco.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: The class will start in very short time.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: {laughs} Wow. We're gonna have so much fun. Ella hablaba como yo.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: She’s speaking like me.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But she’s speaking very perfect gringo Spanish.
{adjusts microphones before class starts}

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Good evening, everybody. Are we okay online? Thank you. Welcome back to the second evening of The Eye of Courage.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: … del Ojo del Valentía.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Wow, she’s having the style. So last night, for me, was really a delight to teach.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: Anoche para mí fue un momento como de "no quiero dar clases." (Last night for me was a moment like "I don't want to teach.")

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: No, no dije esto. Dije otra cosa. (No, I didn't say that. I said something else.)

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: ¿Qué dijiste? (What did you say?)

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Last night was a delight. It was delicious to give this talk. With the friends. Good friends. con los amigos.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And what happened for me is that I was reflecting on the class afterwards, and wondering what happened — like, what happened with me? What was my experience? As you all know, I had a very different class planned. The ideas were there, but it was in a completely different order, a different method of presenting it. And what I realized is that you are my friends. You are my friends, mi compas. My heart opened in class. And I think yours did too. I don't want to assume and pretend that I had your experience, but I think something very magical happened last night. And so the class took on a completely different shape — we were talking about this idea of how we are co-creating this reality together. Like, what did I maybe bring, and what did you bring?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Yes! That's totally broken, Gina. {laughs}

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: Continue, continue.
{adjustments before continuation}

chapters.title: The same seed makes two things

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: We were talking, and there were some really great questions and comments and explorations afterwards, and then this morning as well. So I took some of those questions and built them into today's class.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: We were talking about the ways in which we appear — the ways that we show up in any moment. When I walk in that door, who am I? When you walk through the door, who are you? And we talked really in depth about this: if you show up as a human, there are certain seeds available to you that are only available to you as a human. And if you're a dog, there are certain seeds available to you. So when you see this, the seed opens in your mind to see a pen. When a dog opens their eyes, they see a chew toy.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: It's too bad he's not here, but — I can't remember his name. Luis. Luis gave a very beautiful presentation of the pen this afternoon. It was amazing. And he had so much passion. I was like, that guy is going to be a teacher.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So with that structure — that idea that humans see this kind of thing and a dog sees this kind of thing — we can assume that we have certain seeds and dogs have different seeds. Now, if a human has seeds for a chew toy —

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Luis, you missed my compliment. So I'll do it again. I was saying that Luis gave a beautiful presentation of the pen and chew toy earlier today. And it wasn't just passion — he had clarity too, right?

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So even if you had a seed as a human for a chew toy, as a human you can't get that seed to ripen. Because the way a seed ripens is in two parts: it ripens as you, and it also ripens as the thing that you see. They're not made of separate substances. It's the same seed. So there's you as a human, and this is a pen — it's within the same seed. And because you is a human, you see pen.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And I know it mixes up with two usted in Spanish, and that's not what I mean — tú es humano instead of tú eres humano. ("you is a human" instead of "you are a human.") You is a human because you see a pen. The dog is a dog because they see a chew toy. The same seed creates two different things. Everyone with me? More or less, right? Okay.

chapters.title: Beliefs so deep that you become them

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now we're going to move this into the realm of humans. Same concept, same idea. But now let's talk about what seeds are available to you, in your own particular flavor of you, as a human.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: We talked about the way that you show up, the way you appear to yourself, the way you are you — that determines what things you can and cannot see. And we talked about different examples, the guy who is so worried about money that his entire world is about lack.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So if you have these kinds of deep-seated, deep-rooted beliefs about yourself — and I'm being careful by saying "beliefs," because it's not like you believe it the way you believe in mermaids. It's so deep inside of you that you are that. You can believe in mermaids, you could even think you're a mermaid — and then I throw you in the water, and you're not a mermaid.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I love that Spanish calls them sirenas. From the Odyssey — the sirens. Sirenas are mermaids. A little bit different, but the same roots. Anyway, I'm also a nerd.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I'm using the word "belief," but in a very specific way. It's not that you believe these things about yourself — you are those things. You are those limitations. And then they determine the seeds that can come out. If it’s so deep inside you that the world is built on lack, you’re going to see a world that doesn’t have enough. So the seeds that are available to you, based on your belief systems — that's what we're looking at.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So tonight we're going to explore that, using different words, but keep in mind that those words always mean you. The you that shows up in a moment. The you that arises, of course, coming out of seeds. So we might talk about things in the form of a narrative — the story that you tell yourself.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And this is where I want to start the class, because this came up in a couple of questions last night, and I think it's really important.

chapters.title: Changing the story vs. experiencing the change

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So: "Tim, I have a question. If I change the story, then I change the reality, right? That's what you said." And I said, yes, that's what I said. But it's not exactly what I meant.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: As Luis said earlier — everyone close your eyes. I'm the only one cheating. This pen that's in my hand: I want you to create a story in your mind that I'm not holding a pen, but I'm holding the most valuable diamond, in the shape of a pen, that you can ever imagine. And our motivation is so powerful and pure, because when we open our eyes and see those diamonds, not only will Casa Tartuk be funded for eternity — then we'll have the funds to go build more Casa Tartuks all around Latin America. So we have a very beautiful motivation. Incredible motivation.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All right, everyone's eyes closed. Abre tu corazón.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: Open your heart.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Feel it. Siéntelo. Desire it. Want it. When you open your eyes, if anyone sees a diamond, I want you to raise your hand. On the count of three. One, two, three.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Yeah — we have to do more fundraising for Casa Tartuk.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So when I talk about changing stories, I'm not talking about "tell yourself a different story and then change your reality." Now, that could be part of the process. But there's a difference between thinking about it and experiencing the change. There's a deep, deep difference between sitting in a class, going through some exercises, thinking about it — and having a direct perception.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Where it arises in your experience, that when you open that door, that story is not even available to you. It is gone. That's a completely different level. You actually embody it. You are it. Me is that.
